result.reviewScopeSummary: Verified Story 1 against AC/TC mapping, tech design, implementor artifact, smoothing handler/floor/prompt code, turn composition recovery floor path, retry/terminal queue behavior, and configured gates. One blocking AC-1.3 production-path issue remains.

newFindings.title: Deterministic cleaning mutates fenced code before inference

openFindings.title: Deterministic cleaning mutates fenced code before inference

verified: AC-1.1 / TC-1.1a, TC-1.1b: deterministic cleaning runs before provider work and over-cap prompts still store cleaned output.
AC-1.2 / TC-1.2a, TC-1.2b: under-cap smoothing invokes `smoothPrompt`; over-cap smoothing stores deterministic output with no provider call.
AC-1.4 / TC-1.4a, TC-1.4b: deterministic-only and inference-success smoothing land `ready`; no skipped/degraded state was found.
AC-1.5 / TC-1.5a, TC-1.5b: retryable provider failure leaves `smoothed_prompt` pending and queued; turn composition consumes deterministic floor.
AC-1.6 / TC-1.6a: intake queues `prompt_smoothing` and provider capture remains empty during intake.
AC-1.7 / TC-1.7a, TC-1.7b: exhausted smoothing failure lands `failed` with reason; turn composition consumes deterministic floor.
unverified: AC-1.3 / TC-1.3a: fenced-code byte preservation is contradicted by `cleanPrompt` mutating fenced content before inference.

gatesRun.command: cd packages/lhc && pnpm exec vitest run test/smoothing-recovery.test.ts

productionPathFindings: `smoothPromptHandler` sends globally cleaned text to the provider, so under-cap production smoothing can mutate fenced code before the `smoothing-v1` prompt instruction has any chance to preserve it.
additionalObservations: No material fake-adapter, shim, placeholder, or fallback workaround was found beyond the fenced-code production-path mismatch above.
